The Houston Rockets are road favorites of around eight points tonight at Capital One Arena, but this is a spot where I'd rather take the points with the Washington Wizards . Houston rolls in at 10-3 with three straight wins, including snapping the Warriors' streak , while Washington sits at 4-9 and has dropped six in a row.
 My pick is Washington plus 8.5, and BetMGM has the friendliest price at -110. I still think Houston wins, but I don't trust this group to put a struggling team away by nine or more without their starting point guard. My final score is Rockets 117, Wizards 111.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rockets vs Wizards Odds
 Odds are current as of 3:30 p.m. CT on Sunday, Nov. 15, and subject to change before tipoff.
 DraftKings: Moneyline Rockets -326, Wizards +262. Spread Rockets -8.5 (-103), Wizards +8.5 (-117)
 FanDuel: Moneyline Rockets -350, Wizards +280. Spread Rockets -8.5 (-106), Wizards +8.5 (-112)
 BetMGM: Moneyline Rockets -325, Wizards +260. Spread Rockets -8.5 (-110), Wizards +8.5 (-110)
 Caesars: Moneyline Rockets -345, Wizards +270. Spread Rockets -8 (-115), Wizards +8 (-105)
 Tipoff: 6 p.m. CT at Capital One Arena in Washington.
 TV: Space City Home Network and SCHN+ in Houston.
 Fred VanVleet is out with right knee injury management, per tonight's injury report , since Houston is in Miami tomorrow and they've been protecting his knee on back-to-backs. Marcus Smart also serves the second game of his suspension, which leaves the backcourt thinner than it's been all season and puts a lot of ball handling on Amen Thompson and Reed Sheppard.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Rockets also have a funny habit of playing down to their competition. Utah came into Friday at 1-11 without three of their biggest pieces, yet the Jazz led by as many as 10 and Houston never pulled ahead by more than 12 in a 125-118 win. It took a 43-point night from Alperen Şengün to keep things from getting uncomfortable.
 Washington also brings more firepower than Utah did, with Anthony Davis averaging 25.6 points and 10.5 rebounds, Trae Young is dishing out 8.8 assists a night, and both are available. The Wizards are 2-3 at home, beat Milwaukee and Charlotte by double digits there and pushed Detroit to double overtime on Friday before falling 144-140.
 The biggest risk is Steven Adams, who's available for the first time in 11 games and gives Houston some muscle on the glass against Davis. Washington has also lost their last five by nearly 15 points a game, though a 39-point drubbing in Oklahoma City inflates that number.
 This feels like a sloppy, physical game where Houston does just enough. Without VanVleet, I see a single-digit Rockets win, and I'll happily take those points with Washington.
